item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact Upload API, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption definitions, validates inputs, and tests the required behavior. A introduces multiple expressly forbidden APIs and broad unrelated machinery.","reasons":["B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly with field \"file\" and the supplied filename; A expands the helper and adds unsupported multipart association fields.","B leaves FilesOption behavior and API surface unchanged, while A adds seven association options plus WithFileFormValues, explicitly contrary to the contract.","B includes focused tests for multipart field/name/content, validation, source-reader failures, retry behavior, and os.File-backed Add retries.","Both implementations duplicate Add's request/response logic instead of routing Upload through FilesService.Add, but B's duplication is small and mechanically equivalent; A compounds this with custom option processing and new response logic as well as broader changes."],"risks_a":["Expressly violates scope by adding association fields and new public FilesOption constructors.","Changes RawClient body ownership, content-length handling, seek behavior, and retry semantics across unrelated SDK calls.","Introduces NewFileWithFields and substantial duplicate multipart machinery despite the requirement to reuse NewFile unchanged for this feature request needs only single file part in Upload path (though NewFile is changed to delegate). More importantly, Upload calls NewFileWithFields instead of established helper directly and bypasses Add entirely (it directly calls Raw.Do), duplicating option and response handling instead of centralizing it as required. The changelog/README document forbidden API expansion and behavior changes."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, so future Add changes could diverge from Upload.","The RawClient-wide buffering change is outside the contract's requested scope and changes memory/streaming behavior for every reader body when retries are active.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than an opaque streaming reader, although NewFile's buffering and the os.File Add test provide supporting coverage."]}
